note.zh: 20 世纪神学的重要人物；塑造了对「象征」的理解

note.en: The origin of the modern idea of a leap of faith
note.zh: 现代「信仰跃升」观念的源头

note.en: A standard account of why people surrender freedom voluntarily
note.zh: 关于人为何自愿交出自由的经典论述

note.en: The Theory of Moral Sentiments, on how we see ourselves through others
note.zh: 《道德情操论》，论我们如何透过他人看自己

note.en: Invented the essay; the first sustained study of a self in flux
note.zh: 散文体裁的发明者；第一部持续研究流动自我的作品

note.en: The Ethics of Belief is the standard statement of evidentialism
note.zh: 《信念的伦理》是证据主义的标准陈述

image.credit: William Kingdon Clifford (editors Leslie Stephen and Fredick Pollock)

origin.zh: 尼科波利斯，约公元 125 年

note.en: The Enchiridion has stayed in print for nineteen centuries and carries Stoicism into modern self-help
note.zh: 《手册》流传十九个世纪未曾绝版，也是斯多葛思想进入现代自助读物的主要来源

note.en: A founder of the Arts and Crafts movement and a socialist critic of industrial labour — one of the few to join technology, craft and the meaning of work in one argument
note.zh: 工艺美术运动的奠基者，也是工业劳动的社会主义批评者 — 少数把技术、手艺与劳动意义放在同一个论证里的人

desc.en: Private notes by a Roman emperor on accepting fate and governing himself.
desc.zh: 罗马皇帝关于接受命运与自我治理的私人笔记。

why.en: A working notebook, not a treatise — you watch someone talk himself into accepting what he cannot control.
why.zh: 一本工作笔记而非论著：你会看到一个人如何说服自己接受无法控制之事。

desc.en: A wisdom book on the vanity of effort and the shortness of memory.
desc.zh: 一卷智慧书，论劳碌的虚空与记忆的短暂。

why.en: The bleakest book in the canon, and the one that refuses every easy consolation.
why.zh: 正典中最冷峻的一卷，拒绝一切廉价安慰。

desc.en: An essay on how to live once the world offers no reasons.
desc.zh: 一篇关于世界不提供理由时如何生活的随笔。

why.en: The clearest statement of what to do when explanation runs out and you still have to live.
why.zh: 当解释走到尽头而你仍要活下去时该怎么办 — 最清晰的陈述。

desc.en: A psychiatrist's account of finding meaning in the camps.
desc.zh: 一位精神科医师关于在集中营中寻得意义的记述。

why.en: The case that meaning is found in a situation rather than supplied by the universe.
why.zh: 论意义在处境中被找到，而非由宇宙提供。

desc.en: On labour, work and action, and what it means to appear in public.
desc.zh: 论劳动、工作与行动，以及「在公共中显现」意味着什么。

why.en: Where the argument lives that a life is judged by what it starts, not what it accumulates.
why.zh: 「一生应以其开启之事而非积累之物来衡量」这一论证的出处。

desc.en: An argument that culture is machinery for avoiding mortality.
desc.zh: 论文化是回避死亡的机器。

why.en: An argument that most of culture is machinery for not thinking about mortality.
why.zh: 论大部分文化都是「不去想死亡」的机器。

desc.en: Stories and paradoxes that loosen fixed positions.
desc.zh: 以故事与悖论松动固定立场。

why.en: Stories and paradoxes that unsettle fixed positions rather than replacing them with new ones.
why.zh: 以故事与悖论动摇固定立场，而不是用新立场取代它们。

desc.en: Fragments of Confucius on conduct, ritual and office.
desc.zh: 孔子论行事、礼与为官的片段记录。

why.en: Confucius redirecting metaphysical questions toward conduct, recorded in fragments.
why.zh: 孔子把形而上的问题引向行事，以片段记录下来。

desc.en: The case for individual freedom and its limits.
desc.zh: 为个人自由及其边界辩护。

why.en: Still the sharpest statement of why the majority being sure is not the same as the majority being right.
why.zh: 关于「多数人确信」不等于「多数人正确」的最锐利陈述。

image.credit: John Stuart Mill (author), John W. Parker and Son (publisher)

desc.en: The distinction between freedom from interference and freedom to become.
desc.zh: 区分「免于干涉的自由」与「成为自己的自由」。

why.en: The essay that made it impossible to say 'freedom' without saying which kind.
why.zh: 这篇文章之后，说「自由」就必须说清是哪一种。

desc.en: A novel containing the Grand Inquisitor's case against freedom.
desc.zh: 小说中包含《宗教大法官》对自由的控诉。

why.en: The Grand Inquisitor chapter argues people hand freedom away with relief — read it before deciding you want more.
why.zh: 《宗教大法官》一章论人们如释重负地交出自由 — 在你确信想要更多自由前读它。

desc.en: On how a person is made rather than born into a social role.
desc.zh: 论一个人如何被造就，而非生来就属于某个社会角色。

why.en: The origin of the argument that identity is produced by situation, not discovered in nature.
why.zh: 「身份由处境造就而非在自然中被发现」这一论证的源头。

title.en: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life
title.zh: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life

desc.en: Social life described as staged performance, with front and back regions.
desc.zh: 把社会生活描述为舞台表演，区分前台与后台。

why.en: Once you have read it you cannot stop noticing the performance, including your own.
why.zh: 读过之后，你会不断注意到表演 — 包括你自己的。

desc.en: On identity, continuity and what matters in survival.
desc.zh: 论同一性、连续性，以及存续中真正重要的是什么。

why.en: The thought experiments that make 'am I the same person?' a much harder question than it looks.
why.zh: 一系列思想实验，让「我还是同一个人吗」变得远比看上去困难。

desc.en: Where personal identity is first tied to continuity of memory.
desc.zh: 首次把人格同一性系于记忆的连续性。

why.en: Book II chapter 27 is where the modern conversation about personal identity starts.
why.zh: 第二卷第 27 章是现代人格同一性讨论的起点。

image.credit: The original uploader was Olaf Simons at German Wikipedia.

desc.en: Contains the experience machine, the standard objection to hedonism.
desc.zh: 书中提出「体验机」，对享乐主义的标准反驳。

why.en: One short thought experiment that most people fail, and learn something from failing.
why.zh: 一个简短的思想实验，多数人「答错」，并从答错中有所得。

desc.en: Morality read as a history with interests behind it.
desc.zh: 把道德读作背后带着利益的历史。

why.en: Nietzsche asking not whether a value is true but who it served — a question that does not switch off.
why.zh: 尼采问的不是某价值是否为真，而是它服务于谁 — 这个问题一旦问出便无法关闭。

desc.en: On virtue, habit and what a life well lived consists in.
desc.zh: 论德性、习惯，以及好的一生由什么构成。

why.en: The origin of the idea that character is built by repetition, not chosen in a moment.
why.zh: 「品格由重复养成，而非一念之间选定」这一想法的源头。

desc.en: A forecast that abundance would arrive and leave us short of purpose.
desc.zh: 预测富足终将到来，而我们将缺少目的。

why.en: A century old and now checkable — he got the productivity right and the working week wrong.
why.zh: 写于近百年前，如今可以核对：生产率他猜对了，工时他猜错了。

title.en: The Theory of the Leisure Class
title.zh: The Theory of the Leisure Class

desc.en: On status competition and consumption as display.
desc.zh: 论地位竞争与作为展示的消费。

why.en: Written about the Gilded Age and embarrassingly applicable to now.
why.zh: 写的是镀金时代，读来却尴尬地贴合当下。

desc.en: The account of alienated labour.
desc.zh: 关于异化劳动的论述。

why.en: The alienation argument, before the economics — about what work does to a person.
why.zh: 在经济学之前的异化论证 — 关于劳动对人做了什么。

desc.en: An argument that some questions cannot wait for evidence.
desc.zh: 论有些问题无法等待证据。

why.en: James's argument that some questions are forced, aimed at people who prefer to abstain.
why.zh: 詹姆斯论有些问题是被迫的，专为倾向弃权的人而写。

desc.en: Eighty-one short chapters on acting with the grain of things.
desc.zh: 八十一章短文，讲顺物之纹理而行。

why.en: Short, aphoristic, and the primary source for pattern without a planner.
why.zh: 简短、格言式，是「有规律而无安排者」的原始文本。

desc.en: A plain introduction to no-self and dependent origination.
desc.zh: 关于无我与缘起的平实导论。

why.en: A compact introduction to no-self and dependent origination without much jargon.
why.zh: 关于无我与缘起的简明导论，几乎没有术语。

desc.en: How shared reality is built and then experienced as given.
desc.zh: 共享的现实如何被建构，又如何被体验为理所当然。

why.en: The book that made 'socially constructed' a phrase, for better and worse.
why.zh: 让「社会建构」成为流行说法的那本书 — 有好有坏。

desc.en: Jung's account of coincidences that carry meaning without cause.
desc.zh: 荣格论无因果却有意义的巧合。

why.en: Useful for seeing where the claim is psychological and where it overreaches.
why.zh: 用来看清这一主张在哪里属于心理学，在哪里越界。

desc.en: A dialogue on duty and detachment set on the eve of a battle.
desc.zh: 战前夕关于义务与不执著的对话。

why.en: The origin of the act-without-attachment argument.
why.zh: 「行动而不执著于结果」这一论证的源头。

desc.en: On symbol, and why a religious claim is not a factual report.
desc.zh: 论象征，以及宗教主张为何不是事实报告。

why.en: The clearest statement that taking a symbol literally is the way to misunderstand it.
why.zh: 「按字面理解象征即是误解象征」最清晰的陈述。

desc.en: Why people hand freedom to authority, written as it was happening.
desc.zh: 人为何把自由交给权威 — 写于此事正在发生之时。

why.en: Written in 1941 about why people choose submission — the timing is the argument.
why.zh: 写于 1941 年，论人为何选择服从 — 写作时机本身就是论证。

desc.en: The book whose reception cost Russell a teaching post.
desc.zh: 这本书的反响让罗素失去了一个教职。

why.en: Contains his flattest line about how little popularity proves.
why.zh: 书中有他最直白的一句：流行说明不了什么。

desc.en: On sympathy, and the impartial spectator we build inside ourselves.
desc.zh: 论同情，以及我们在内心建立的公正旁观者。

why.en: The other Smith — on why we cannot stop watching ourselves being watched.
why.zh: 另一个斯密 — 论我们为何无法停止看着自己被看。

desc.en: A man studying himself over twenty years and finding no fixed thing.
desc.zh: 一个人用二十年研究自己，却找不到固定之物。

why.en: The first writer to treat his own inconsistency as the finding rather than the failure.
why.zh: 第一位把自身的不一致当作发现而非失败的作者。

desc.en: On how much confidence the evidence actually licenses.
desc.zh: 论证据究竟容许多少确信。

why.en: Opens with a proposal so demanding Russell admits it would be revolutionary.
why.zh: 开篇提出的要求之高，连罗素自己都承认是革命性的。

desc.en: An argument that believing without evidence is a moral failure, not just an error.
desc.zh: 论无证据而信是道德过失，而不只是错误。

why.en: The shipowner parable at the start does more work than the argument that follows.
why.zh: 开篇的船主寓言比后面的论证更有力。

desc.en: The notebooks where his idea of a truth one can live by first appears.
desc.zh: 「可据以生活的真理」这一想法最早出现的笔记。

why.en: Written at twenty-two, and already the whole programme is there.
why.zh: 写于二十二岁，整个纲领已在其中。

desc.en: On the goodness of human nature and what circumstance does to it.
desc.zh: 论人性之善，以及环境对它做了什么。

why.en: The water metaphor is the clearest ancient statement of nature versus circumstance.
why.zh: 水的比喻是关于「本性与环境」最清晰的古代陈述。

desc.en: On the city, and why a human outside one is not fully human.
desc.zh: 论城邦，以及为何人在城邦之外不成其为完整的人。

why.en: Where belonging is argued to be constitutive rather than optional.
why.zh: 归属在此被论证为构成性的，而非可选的。

desc.en: A defence of welfare as the measure, with room for higher pleasures.
desc.zh: 为以福利作为尺度辩护，并为高级快乐留出位置。

why.en: The dissatisfied-Socrates passage is where Mill breaks with simple hedonism.
why.zh: 「不满足的苏格拉底」一段，是密尔与简单享乐主义分道之处。

title.en: An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation
title.zh: An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation

desc.en: The founding statement of utilitarian calculation.
desc.zh: 功利计算的奠基性陈述。

why.en: The opening sentence is the whole doctrine in one line.
why.zh: 开篇一句就是整套学说。

desc.en: The line-judgement experiments, reported by the man who ran them.
desc.zh: 线段判断实验，由实验者本人报告。

why.en: Short, plain, and the numbers are still uncomfortable seventy years later.
why.zh: 简短平实，七十年后那些数字依然令人不安。

title.en: The Point of View for My Work as an Author
title.zh: The Point of View for My Work as an Author

desc.en: Kierkegaard explaining, after the fact, what he had been doing.
desc.zh: 克尔凯郭尔事后解释自己一直在做什么。

why.en: Contains his flattest statement about crowds, and it is not a compliment.
why.zh: 书中有他关于群众最直白的一句 — 那不是赞美。
